text:
mia: quick RFC follow-up on on-prem upgrade flow. proposing we formalize a serializer-version header + a tiny backstop verifier image so deltas can be encoded with capability-aware encodings and nodes that can’t handle the new encoding fall back safely. goal = deterministic partial-replay + safe rollbacks across reboots.

raj: sounds reasonable. what's the concrete benefit of a serializer token vs adding compatibility code to the agent runtime?

mia: serializer token keeps agent runtime minimal. delta payloads declare their encoding (e.g. serializer=v1 | v2). controller routes deltas based on `GET /capabilities`. if agent doesn’t support the serializer, controller uses full-image swap or instructs agent to pull the backstop image. avoids shipping multiple shims in the agent.

sam: full-image swap is costly for large fleets. what size are we talking for the backstop image and how does operator UX look?

mia: backstop = minimal verifier + replayer + health probe ~110-140MB gz depending on base. It only needs enough to validate manifest headers and replay chunked payloads into the on-disk blobstore. Operator UX: installer can pre-pull backstop, then controller can request `POST /pull-backstop?manifest=<sha256>` before applying deltas.

elaine: we need a capability discovery contract. proposal: `GET /capabilities` -> {"serializers":["v1","v2"], "apply_modes":["swap","stream"]}. Controller includes `X-Serializer: v2` on `POST /delta`. Simple negotiation.

jules: +1. also add a field in the release notes and a matrix in the console showing which clusters still need backstop. ops will love a clear graph.

raj: tradeoffs: adding per-chunk sha256 increases manifest size ~10%, but enables resumable partial apply and aggressive GC of staged blobs. We should prefer chunk checksums for long-term reliability.

mia: proposal for manifest version 3 minimal schema: fields as plain strings/lists -> serializer, manifest_version=3, chunks=[{sha256,size}], backstop_uri (optional), apply_mode=(swap|stream), signer_key_id. keep it intentionally minimal to reduce parser complexity on agents.

sam: apply_mode=stream vs swap: stream uses constant disk write and low peak disk but is hard to abort safely. swap writes into a tmp layout and atomically renames; higher disk footprint but simpler rollback semantics.

elaine: default to swap for safety. allow stream behind an operator flag for constrained devices. console should surface a preflight check when stream is requested.

ops-bot: rollout-scan: staging: 3/24 nodes reported serializer=v1-only. staged delta with serializer=v2 will fallback to swap/pull-backstop for those nodes.

nikhil: request: add `/healthz?manifest=<sha256>` on backstop image. It should validate manifest header and basic chunk availability without performing the full apply. return 200 + small JSON with capabilities. installers can call it post-pull to assert integrity.

mia: noted. action items: (1) spec `/capabilities` & `X-Serializer` header (2) implement manifest-v3 encoder in packager (3) bake backstop image variant + health endpoint, publish artifact manifest (4) console UX: rollout modal displays compatibility window + warn when nodes lack serializer v2.

raj: compatibility policy proposal: mixed-cluster support for 14 days post-release. after window expires, new deltas requiring v2 are rejected and console surfaces required backstop pull. put that in release notes and enterprise SLA docs.

jules: add an automated job that scans registered clusters and emails ops owners with a countdown when they fall behind. also add link to `redwoodctl` commands in the modal.

sam: sample CLI snippets for ops: `redwoodctl agent-capabilities --host 10.0.5.12` and `redwoodctl push-delta --serializer v2 --file delta.tar.zst` — include in docs.

elaine: i'll own docs + console copy. mia, can you draft the RFC patch with manifest examples and the backstop health-check contract? tag me for copy review.

mia: yes. i'll draft RFC patch and include a minimal JSON manifest example and the `GET /capabilities`/`POST /delta` sketches. will tag @jules @raj @elaine for review. thanks everyone. :thumbsup:
